body:
MAINLINE-018. Knockdown 1 on the shear-crimp branch is the NASA CR-1457 rule, not a sphere test. Section 6.2.2 sets hemisphere Yd to 0.20 below Vc 2 and to 1 at Vc >= 2. The theory is Yao 1962 as rewritten by Plantema 1966. Page 6-7 says weak cores are insensitive to imperfections and that a continuous transition is beyond the handbook. Dome data are the scarce Saturn S-II set, Gonzalez and Patton, SDL 468, 1964. The 0.20 is explicitly except where shear crimping occurs. Axial cylinder tests, March and Kuenzi 1957 and a 1963 Hexcel summary, mostly beat that prediction; one reached 0.86. That transfer is QUESTIONABLE.

Wagner 2020 Table 3 has no sandwich row. SP-8032 is a monocoque cap. SP-8007 was not opened. Plantema was not opened beyond the citation.

Sim et al. 2024 give numerical imperfect/perfect factors 0.20 and 0.22. Their flat hemisphere, from EUCASS 2023-367 Figure 4, has handbook Vc 201.532463528 with G taken as E/2. That shell is on the crimp branch. The denominator is their own linear load, not CR-1457.

Optimistic curve, PROJECTION: gamma = 0.20 + 0.40*min(Vc, 2). It leaves the crimp branch at 1. Conservative curve: gamma = 0.20 at every Vc. Neither stacks another knockdown.

Held geometry. Optimistic least factors: Be/HRH 0.685338231171, core shear crimping; K13D2U 0.651932173894, face wrinkling; AlBeMet 0.553994420508, face wrinkling; SiC/Divinycell 0.235167984044, face wrinkling. Conservative: Be 0.137067646234, K13D2U 0.13045040032, AlBeMet 0.110868173353, all core shear crimping; SiC stays 0.23515931325, global buckling. P3 stays PENDING-011b. Not a certification.
